title: Tolerant streaming JSON: chunk coalescing, escape-normalization, truncated-field repair & deterministic retry semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Streaming structured JSON responses are subject to chunk boundaries that can split UTF-8 sequences, escape sequences (\" and \\uXXXX), and object/array tokens. Current strict parsers either fail the stream or trigger full-response fallbacks, causing higher latency and poor developer experience. We also need deterministic semantics when retries occur for tool/function-calls embedded in streams (avoid double-execution, ensure idempotency).

Goal: Implement a tolerant streaming JSON handling layer that: 1) coalesces adjacent chunks and normalizes partial escape/UTF-8 sequences, 2) attempts best-effort repair for truncated fields (with clear provenance), 3) provides a compact fallback envelope for unrecoverable fragments, and 4) defines deterministic retry semantics and idempotency hints for tool/function calls emitted mid-stream. This should preserve existing APIs while adding opt-in compatibility flags for stricter consumers.

Scope: Parser/runtime changes, protocol-level streaming envelope additions, SDK client helpers (JS/Python) to surface repaired fragments and recovery metadata, test harness and fuzzing for chunk-split edge cases. Not in scope: changing model tokenization or generator-side guarantees (we add server/client-side mitigation).
acceptance_criteria: Streaming responses with split UTF-8 multibyte sequences across chunks are reassembled transparently and parsed as valid JSON in tolerant mode
Broken/partial escape sequences (e.g., truncated \" or \\uXXXX) are corrected when possible; when correction is ambiguous, stream emits a well-documented 'repaired_string' marker in metadata
When object/array structure is truncated in-flight, runtime emits a minimal reconcile envelope (type: 'partial-repair' or 'final-abort') rather than silently failing, and SDK surfaces this to callers
Function/tool-call messages embedded in streams include an idempotency token when emitted; retries use deterministic replay semantics to avoid duplicate side effects by default
New behavior is behind opt-in flags: 'stream_tolerance=v1' on the API and 'tolerant_streaming' in SDKs; default remains strict for customers who rely on byte-for-byte output
Unit + integration tests cover 30+ chunk-splitting permutations including multibyte UTF-8, escaped quotes, nested arrays, and mid-stream tool-call messages
Rollout plan documented with metrics: parsing-error-rate, fallback-rate, repaired-fragment-rate, tool-call-duplicate-rate
Performance overhead measured and capped: extra latency p50 increase <= 3ms on average for tolerant mode under normal workloads
discussion: 2026-02-16 - Marco Nguyen: Initial investigation shows most failures come from naive streaming parsers that immediately feed chunks to strict JSON.parse. We can buffer up to N bytes and attempt normalized reassembly. Need to pick a safe max-buffer-size to avoid OOM.
2026-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Product insists behavior be opt-in. Add API flag and SDK toggle. We'll also provide a recovery metadata field so downstream apps can decide how to present repaired text.
2026-02-22 - Kiran Rao (runtime): Prototyped a C++ incremental parser that can detect incomplete escape sequences and multibyte splits; repair rules look OK but ambiguous cases need audit trail.
2026-02-28 - Design (Elena Torres): UX patterns for repaired fragments: show a subtle inline indicator and a link to 'view raw' for strict inspection. Avoid alarming messages for minor repairs.

2026-03-03 - Security (J. Meyer): Need to ensure repaired strings don't enable injection vectors. Confirmed policy: repaired fragments are marked in metadata and always escaped when surfaced to callers. Security review checklist added.
decisions: Implement a two-tier tolerant parser: a small bounded coalescing buffer (default 8KB) for immediate chunk stitching, and a fallback reparative pass with explicit metadata when topology is still invalid
Expose an API-level flag 'stream_tolerance' with values 'off'|'coalesce'|'repair' where 'repair' emits repaired_fragment metadata

For tool/function calls, require an 'idempotency_token' emitted by the model producer when possible; if absent, server will synthesize a deterministic token using (request_id, chunk_sequence, function_name) and emit it with the function call message
SDKs will surface repaired fragments via an event 'onRepairedFragment({path, original_bytes, repaired_string, repair_reason})'
Keep strict mode as default for existing customers; new customers may opt-in via console or request header

notes: Edge-case: models that intentionally emit partial JSON fragments for human-in-the-loop editing. We will expose a 'finality' marker in the envelope so such flows can use explicit patch messages instead of repair heuristics.
Consider adding a header 'x-stream-raw-checksum' in future to allow clients to verify raw byte fidelity when needed
Keep monitoring for user-visible regressions; add an alert if repaired_fragment_rate > 0.5% for a customer
